findings.summary: MAX_CLUES=24 is declared in the e0-regression profile and parsed by tick-entry --max-clues, but the production assembly chain never carries it to the tick: fleet.yaml.tpl does not inject max_clues into pipeline input (no max_clues: ${MAX_CLUES} line alongside max_writes/triage_threshold at lines 12/25), and tick.md never reads max_clues nor appends --max-clues to tick_args (compare --max-writes at tick.md:25,51). In production the tick therefore falls back to DEFAULT_TICK_CONFIG.maxClues=64, so the regression research scope is not actually narrowed. This re-introduces the exact defect the prior rf- blocker flagged (profiles/deploy/e0-regression.env:44-61): nothing in the delivery narrows the regression scope, so 判据 6's self-consistency demand (2400s wall clock must reach a non-null termination) is unaddressed. The profile comment at e0-regression.env:64 ('入口 bin/e0-regression.sh 加载后写入环境，tick-entry --run 经 --max-clues 传给 tick') is false — the assembly chain that would carry it does not exist.

判据 4b's discriminating test does not verify the production wiring. test/e0c7-node-timeout.test.ts:548-595 passes maxClues:24 directly to runChannelWrite in the test harness, bypassing the fleet.yaml.tpl → tick.md → tick-entry --run assembly chain entirely. This is the pattern spec §5 explicitly warns against ('测试绕开被测入口、在测试内部重实现一遍逻辑'): the test proves the TS API accepts a maxClues value, not that the profile-declared MAX_CLUES ever reaches the production tick. Reverting the (non-existent) production wiring leaves this test green, so it is not discriminating for the actual defect.
